name: BMW 2002 tii
engine: 2.0L M10 SOHC inline-four with Kugelfischer PL04 mechanical fuel injection
torque: ~131 lb-ft @ ~4,500 rpm (DIN; US SAE-net rated ~125 hp)
transmission: 4-speed manual (a close-ratio 5-speed Getrag was a rare option, mostly outside the US)
fuel_economy: ~24–30 mpg (period; a well-tuned tii can see ~35 mpg on the highway)
reliability: 8/10 — the tii is the fuel-injected flagship of the 02 series, and its simple, sturdy M10 four is famously long-lived; a healthy one is a wonderfully honest, tossable classic. The two ownership realities are era-appropriate. First, the Kugelfischer mechanical injection pump is finicky and specialist-dependent — set correctly it's crisp and reliable, but a poorly-adjusted or long-stored pump loses power and drivability, and rust or debris in the fuel system will foul it. Second, like any 1970s car, rust is the real enemy. Find a rust-free, properly-fueled tii and it will reward you for decades.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Low–Moderate on an agreed-value classic policy · Maintenance ~$800/yr, plus a Kugelfischer specialist on call · Values of clean, correct tiis are strong and rising — this is a beloved blue-chip vintage BMW
popular_mods: A correctly rebuilt and dialed-in Kugelfischer pump — the heart of a good-running tii
A thorough fuel-system cleanup (tank, lines, filters) to protect the injection
Careful, reversible rust repair — the single most value-preserving work on any 02
Period-correct suspension refresh and a 5-speed swap for relaxed cruising (kept reversible)
Honest take: keep it correct and rust-free — a numbers-matching, properly-injected tii is worth far more than a modified one

generations.2002 tii (1972–1974): The fuel-injected flagship of the 02 range — 'touring international injection' — pairing the light 2002 body with the Kugelfischer mechanical pump for crisp throttle response and genuine sporting character. Widely credited as the car that built BMW's sport-sedan reputation in America and the spiritual ancestor of the 3 Series.
generations.02 series context: The broader 02 range (1966–1976) spanned the carbureted 1600/2002 up to the turbocharged 2002 Turbo; the tii is the injected sweet spot most enthusiasts covet.

common_issues: Kugelfischer injection pump tuning is finicky and specialist-dependent — a poorly-set pump loses power and drivability
Pump internals gum up after long storage due to the oil-recirculation design
Rust in the fuel tank and lines contaminating the pump and injectors
Chronic body rust — rockers, floors, shock towers, and trunk (typical of the era)
M10 timing-chain/guide wear and carbon on injection-related components
maintenance_tips: Use a Kugelfischer specialist — a correctly-set pump is the difference between a great and a gutless tii
Keep the fuel system clean; drive the car regularly so the pump doesn't gum up from sitting
Inspect relentlessly for rust and address it early with correct, reversible repairs
Service the M10 timing chain and keep the valves adjusted — the engine itself is very durable
Preserve originality and numbers-matching parts — correctness drives the strong values

engine.detail: The M10 — BMW's legendarily durable 2.0L SOHC canted 'slant-four,' chain-driven, making 130 hp DIN (US SAE-net ~125 hp) and ~131 lb-ft at ~4,500 rpm. Simple, sturdy, and famously long-lived.
engine.watch: Very durable if maintained — watch the timing chain and guides for wear and keep the valves adjusted; carbon can build on the injection-related components.

fuel.detail: The tii's defining feature: a Kugelfischer PL04 mechanical injection pump in place of carburetors, giving crisp throttle response and the car its 'touring international injection' name.
fuel.watch: The pump is finicky and specialist-dependent — a poorly-set or long-stored pump loses power and drivability, its internals gum up from sitting (the oil-recirculation design), and rust or debris from the tank and lines will foul it. A correctly rebuilt, dialed-in pump is the heart of a good tii.

drivetrain.detail: 4-speed manual driving the rear wheels; a close-ratio 5-speed Getrag was a rare option, mostly outside the US.
drivetrain.watch: Tough and simple — many owners fit the 5-speed for relaxed cruising, ideally kept reversible to preserve originality and value.

suspension.detail: MacPherson-strut front and semi-trailing-arm independent rear — light and tossable, the template for the BMW sport sedan.
suspension.watch: Refresh tired bushings, dampers, and the steering box on any survivor; the payoff is the classic, communicative 02 feel.

brakes.detail: Front discs and rear drums — modest by modern standards but well matched to a ~2,200-2,380 lb car.
brakes.watch: Fine when healthy; keep the hydraulics and flexible lines fresh on a car that's now 50-plus years old.

body.detail: Light steel unibody two-door — the compact shape credited with building BMW's US sport-sedan reputation and the spiritual ancestor of the 3 Series.
body.watch: Rust is the real enemy — rockers, floors, shock towers, and trunk are the chronic spots; a rust-free, numbers-matching car is worth far more than a modified one.
